body.statement: If \(Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\) are independent and identically distributed real random variables with \(E[Z_1]=0\) and \(0<E[Z_1^2]<\infty\), then \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\Rightarrow N(0,E[Z_1^2])\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let Y₁, …, Yₙ be i.i.d. random variables with E Y₁ = 0 and E Y₁² = 1. Then √n Ȳₙ converges in distribution to the standard normal distribution.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the authorized Asymptotic Statistics preview, page 16 of Chapter 2 (PDF preview page 33): https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781107266308_A23760354/preview-9781107266308_A23760354.pdf. The run statement is the variance-rescaled form.
